verses.text: For this cause I, Paul, am the prisoner of Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles,
if it is so that you have heard of the administration of that grace of God which was given me toward you;
how that by revelation the mystery was made known to me, as I wrote before in few words,
by which, when you read, you can perceive my understanding in the mystery of Christ;
which in other generations was not made known to the children of men, as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit;
that the Gentiles are fellow heirs, and fellow members of the body, and fellow partakers of his promise in Christ Jesus through the Good News,
of which I was made a servant, according to the gift of that grace of God which was given me according to the working of his power.
To me, the very least of all saints, was this grace given, to preach to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,
and to make all men see what is the administration  of the mystery which for ages has been hidden in God, who created all things through Jesus Christ;
to the intent that now through the assembly the manifold wisdom of God might be made known to the principalities and the powers in the heavenly places,
according to the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord;
in whom we have boldness and access in confidence through our faith in him.
Therefore I ask that you may not lose heart at my troubles for you, which are your glory.
For this cause, I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named,
that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, that you may be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inward man;
that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith; to the end that you, being rooted and grounded in love,
may be strengthened to comprehend with all the saints what is the width and length and height and depth,
and to know Christ’s love which surpasses knowledge, that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
Now to him who is able to do exceedingly abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that works in us,
to him be the glory in the assembly and in Christ Jesus to all generations forever and ever. Amen.

footnotes.content: Paul calls himself 'the prisoner of Christ Jesus'—a beautiful flip of how the world sees chains. He's in chains for preaching to Gentiles, yet he speaks of it not as loss but as belonging. The Lord had claimed him wholly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul assumes they've heard about God's grace poured out through him. Notice he doesn't boast—he points to the grace. That's the mark of a man who knows his own smallness next to what God is doing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: By revelation, the mystery came to Paul. He mentions he wrote of it briefly before—a real anchor to other letters. What a gift: to understand God's hidden purposes and then put them in writing for folks like us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul invites his readers to perceive his understanding when they read. There's such humility here—he's not saying 'believe what I say' but 'read, and you'll see I understand the mystery of Christ.' The text itself becomes the proof.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: For ages, this truth was hidden—Gentiles as heirs alongside Jews. That old dividing wall seemed eternal to the world, yet God had a plan all along. What looked impossible was always part of His heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fellow heirs, fellow members, fellow partakers. Paul stacks the word 'fellow' to drive home something staggering: Gentiles and Jews, one body, one promise, one Christ. The gospel tears down the highest walls of human division.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A servant through grace—not because Paul earned it or deserved it, but because God's power worked in him. He's simply the vessel through which something far larger than himself moved. That's the only honest way to serve.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The very least of all saints—Paul's humility is real and deep. He knows his own sin, his own smallness. Yet to him was given grace to preach riches unsearchable. Weakness becomes the stage for God's treasures.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The mystery hidden for ages in God—suddenly made known through the Good News. All creation came through Jesus. This isn't new information tacked on; it was woven into the fabric of things from the beginning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The church—ordinary gathered believers—becomes the stage where God displays His wisdom to cosmic powers. How stunning: angels and spirits witness Christ's plan through us. We are living epistles read by heaven itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eternal purpose purposed in Christ Jesus—this wasn't an afterthought or plan B. Before the foundations, the Lord knew, decided, intended. To live in Christ is to live in alignment with what the universe was made for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Boldness and access in confidence through faith—words that shake off fear and shame. We come as we are, known fully, loved fully. No trembling at the door. Faith opens it straight to the Father's heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul grieves that they might lose heart because of his troubles. Yet he reframes: his chains are 'your glory'—not in the sense of spectacle, but of witness, of proof that faith holds fast even when everything says let go.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He bows his knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ—a posture of prayer. Kneeling is his first move, his reflex. Before asking, before speaking, the body bows. That's worship in its truest form.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every family in heaven and on earth is named from the Father. All kinship, all belonging, traces back to Him. When we say 'family,' we're using His word—borrowed from His nature, His infinite capacity to love and hold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Strengthened with power through the Spirit in the inward man—not outward show, but inner steel. The deep self, the real you, grows strong. That's where battles are won and love is learned.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Christ dwelling in your hearts through faith, rooted and grounded in love—a house becomes a home when Someone loved lives there. Roots go deep, foundations hold. We're not blown about by every wind when Christ inhabits us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Width and length and height and depth—cosmic dimensions. Paul is painting the immensity of something too vast for one person alone; we need the saints together to begin to grasp it. Together we grow into fuller sight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Christ's love surpasses knowledge—we can know it experientially, but never measure it completely. Knowledge fails. Love remains. We're filled with all the fullness of God not through understanding, but through surrender to that inexhaustible grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Exceedingly abundantly above all we ask or think—the Lord doesn't just meet us; He exceeds every hope we dare to voice. His power works in us, not despite our weakness but through it, amplifying what we thought impossible.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Glory in the assembly and in Christ Jesus to all generations forever and ever. Readers today hear an echo of this: the Lord is still building His church, still revealing His wisdom through ordinary people gathered in His name. We're part of this endless praise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
